title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Bitbucket Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Bitbucket Cloud SaaS; workspace/project access tokens and IP allowlisting need Premium, org-level audit log needs Atlassian Guard; API tokens are Atlassian-account tokens shared with Jira/Confluence.

controls.name: Delete OAuth consumer
controls.what: Deleting the consumer removes all tokens issued to it.

controls.name: Restrict access to certain IP addresses
controls.what: Only allowlisted IPs can view private content or clone/push/pull private repos.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > Access controls > Restrict access to certain IP addresses

controls_unknown: Whether the workspace IP allowlist is enforced on REST API calls (docs only mention viewing content and Git clone/push/pull).
Whether API tokens or OAuth tokens are checked against IdP SSO or conditional access at use time.
Whether the workspace audit log records access token creation, rotation or revocation (no such events listed).
Lifetime of the Pipelines OIDC token.
OAuth access token lifetime: developer docs say 1 hour, support docs say 2 hours.
Any admin approval workflow for users authorizing third-party OAuth consumers.

authentication.summary: Workspace-registered consumer (key + secret). Authorization code grant acts as the authorizing user; client credentials grant acts as the consumer owner. Access tokens are Bearer tokens to api.bitbucket.org and can clone via x-token-auth.

federation.details: Docs do not say whether IdP session policies are re-checked on refresh.

ip_restriction.boundary: Premium private-content allowlist; API enforcement not documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 1h (support docs say 2h); refresh token expires after 3 months unused

renewal.expiry_basis: refresh token rotates on use; 3-month inactivity expiry
renewal.summary: Refresh without user interaction; client credentials can mint new tokens with the secret.

administration.summary: Workspace admins create and delete consumers in Workspace settings > OAuth consumers; deleting removes all its tokens. Scopes are fixed on the consumer.
administration.conditions: No documented admin approval flow for user authorizations of third-party consumers.

inventory.details: Workspace settings > OAuth consumers lists consumers created in that workspace; no list of issued tokens or user authorizations.

expiry.api: Access token lifetime fixed at 1 hour; renew with POST https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token grant_type=refresh_token

usage.ui: Workspace settings > Security: Audit log; filter events 'User account access granted to an application' / 'revoked'

lifecycle_events.event: User account access granted to an application
User account access to an application revoked

anomaly_cues: Client credentials consumer owned by an admin

containment.steps: Delete the consumer in Workspace settings > OAuth consumers (kills all its tokens); or rotate secret.
containment.notes: Deletion removes all existing tokens linked to the consumer.
